items.title: Every change is built, tested and shipped safely
items.description_md: As the delivery team, we want each commit to the API and web repositories to be built, tested, scanned and deployed through one repeatable pipeline, so that Release 1 can be shipped on 1 March 2027 without manual, error-prone steps and a bad release can be undone quickly. **Why this priority**: Every other feature depends on a working pipeline, and the go-live date is firm (NFR-009). Without it nothing can reach staging or production. **Independent Test**: Push a trivial commit to the API repository and to the web repository. Confirm each pipeline runs every stage in order, a deliberately failing test or a seeded HIGH vulnerability stops the pipeline before deployment, and a deliberately failing health check triggers a rollback to the previous release. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a commit to the API repository, **When** the pipeline runs, **Then** it builds, runs unit tests, runs contract tests against the published API contract, scans the image, deploys to staging, runs the smoke test (health, sign-in with a test code, book and cancel against sandbox providers) and only then replaces production one replica at a time behind the health check. 2. **Given** a failing unit test, a contract test that no longer matches the API contract, or a HIGH image-scan finding, **When** the pipeline runs, **Then** the pipeline stops and nothing is deployed to staging or production. 3. **Given** a commit to the web repository, **When** the pipeline runs, **Then** the web app is built and published separately from the API and the previous published build is kept. 4. **Given** a new release in production, **When** the health check fails, or server errors exceed 2% for 5 minutes, or reminder lag exceeds 15 minutes, **Then** the team can roll back by redeploying the previous API image and the previous web build, and the rollback steps are documented and rehearsed once in staging. 5. **Given** a database change in a release, **When** the pipeline deploys it, **Then** the change only adds or relaxes structures (expand) and stays compatible with the previous release; removals happen in a later release (contract). ---

user_story.i_want: each commit to the API and web repositories built, tested, scanned and deployed through one repeatable pipeline with a rehearsed rollback
user_story.so_that: Release 1 can ship on 1 March 2027 without manual, error-prone steps and a bad release can be undone quickly

items.title: Dev, staging and production environments with managed secrets
items.description_md: As the delivery team, we want separate dev, staging and production environments, each with the API, the web app and the database, and with secrets kept in a secret store, so that we can test safely and production stays available and protected. **Why this priority**: Staging is where the smoke tests and UAT run; production must be ready well before 1 March 2027. **Independent Test**: Create each environment from the infrastructure repository, deploy a build of the API and of the web app to it, call the health check through the public route, and confirm that no secret value appears in any repository, image or log. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the infrastructure repository, **When** an environment is created, **Then** dev, staging and production each host the web app (static, behind a CDN), the API and the database, with dev and staging on the smallest tiers and staging using sandbox accounts for the SMS and WhatsApp providers. 2. **Given** production, **When** a visitor opens the site, **Then** the web app is served from the CDN, requests under `/api` are routed through the load balancer and web application firewall to the API, and all traffic uses HTTPS. 3. **Given** production, **When** one API replica or one zone is lost, **Then** the other replica keeps serving online booking, and under sustained CPU above 60% the API scales between 2 and 4 replicas. 4. **Given** the secret store holds the database credentials, provider keys, webhook secrets and token signing key, **When** the API starts in any environment, **Then** it receives them as environment variables and no secret is present in code, images or configuration files. 5. **Given** the clinic has not yet confirmed a hosting provider or domain, **When** environments are created, **Then** they use an India cloud region chosen by the delivery team and a placeholder domain until the clinic supplies theirs (Assumed: see open question Q1). ---

user_story.i_want: separate dev, staging and production environments, each with the API, web app and database, with secrets kept in a secret store
user_story.so_that: we can test safely and production stays available and protected

items.title: Database baseline, migrations, backups and a tested restore
items.description_md: As the delivery team, we want a managed database with a first migration, a repeatable migration process, encrypted backups and a rehearsed restore, so that appointment data is never lost beyond 15 minutes and service can be restored within 1 hour. **Why this priority**: Every feature stores data in the database, and a tested restore is a go-live condition. **Independent Test**: Run the migrations on an empty database in dev, confirm the baseline schema and the no-overlap capability are present; then restore a production-like database from a snapshot plus archived logs to a chosen point in time and measure the time taken. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an empty database in any environment, **When** the migrations are applied, **Then** the baseline schema is created, including the extension needed to prevent overlapping appointments for one dentist, and the migration can be applied again without error. 2. **Given** the application's database user, **When** it connects, **Then** it can read and write data but cannot change the database structure; structure changes run under a separate migration user. 3. **Given** production, **When** one day passes, **Then** a snapshot is taken and kept 14 days, backups and archived logs are encrypted, and logs are archived continuously so any point in time can be restored. 4. **Given** a backup, **When** the delivery team restores it to a new database before go-live, **Then** the restored data is at most 15 minutes older than the chosen point (RPO) and the restore completes within 1 hour (RTO); the date, duration and result are recorded in the readiness checklist. 5. **Given** production, **When** the primary database node fails, **Then** the synchronous standby in the second zone takes over without losing committed data. ---

user_story.i_want: a managed database with a first migration, a repeatable migration process, encrypted backups and a rehearsed restore
user_story.so_that: appointment data is never lost beyond 15 minutes and service can be restored within 1 hour

items.title: A patient uses every screen comfortably on a phone
items.description_md: As a patient on a phone, I want a plain, mobile-friendly website that needs no install and has big tap targets and no sideways scrolling, so that I can book at any age in Chrome or Safari on my Android phone or iPhone. **Why this priority**: Online booking is the product's main value; the shell sets the layout and rules every patient screen reuses (NFR-001, NFR-010). **Independent Test**: Open the shell's sample patient screens in current Chrome and Safari on an Android phone and an iPhone (real devices or the team's device lab); check for horizontal scrolling, measure tap targets, and count the screens in the booking journey after sign-in. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the web app shell, **When** I open any patient screen on a phone-width display in current Chrome or Safari on Android or iPhone, **Then** the page fits the width with no sideways scrolling and nothing needs to be installed. 2. **Given** any tappable control on a patient screen (buttons, links, form fields, list rows), **When** its size is measured, **Then** it is at least 44 px by 44 px. 3. **Given** the booking journey defined in the shell (who and what, slot picker, confirm, booked), **When** screens are counted after sign-in, **Then** a new patient reaches a booked appointment in 5 screens or fewer. 4. **Given** an automated responsive check, **When** the pipeline runs, **Then** it fails any patient screen that scrolls sideways or has a tap target smaller than 44 px. 5. **Given** a patient with slow 4G, **When** the shell loads, **Then** the sign-in screen is usable without waiting for unrelated screens (the app loads only what the screen needs). ---

user_story.so_that: I can book at any age in Chrome or Safari on my Android phone or iPhone

items.title: All screens and messages are in English with times in India time
items.description_md: As a patient or receptionist, I want every screen and message in plain English and every time shown in India time (IST), so that I never have to convert times or guess what a message means. **Why this priority**: Every later feature shows dates and times; the rule has to exist before screens multiply. **Independent Test**: Store a known moment in time in the database, display it on a patient screen and a reception screen, and compare it to the expected IST clock time, including a moment near midnight and a moment in UTC that falls on a different calendar day in India. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a time stored in universal time (UTC), **When** it is shown on any screen or in any message, **Then** it appears as India time (IST, UTC+05:30) with the correct date, including when the UTC date and the IST date differ. 2. **Given** any screen text or message wording, **When** it is reviewed, **Then** it comes from one English message catalogue and no text is typed directly into a screen or message. 3. **Given** a person enters a date or time in a form, **When** it is saved, **Then** it is interpreted as IST and stored as UTC. 4. **Given** the automated checks, **When** a string is missing from the catalogue or a screen shows a time without a timezone conversion, **Then** the check fails. ---

user_story.i_want: every screen and message in plain English and every time shown in India time (IST)
user_story.so_that: I never have to convert times or guess what a message means

items.title: Reception and the practice manager get a desktop layout that is available in clinic hours
items.description_md: As a receptionist or the practice manager on a desktop browser, I want a wide-screen layout with navigation for my role, available during clinic hours, so that I can run the day from the reception PC. **Why this priority**: Reception screens must be available 08:00 to 20:00 Monday to Saturday; later features add the screens, this story provides the layout and the availability proof. **Independent Test**: Open the staff area on a desktop browser at common desktop widths and confirm it uses the space; run the availability probe for the reception screens over a clinic day. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a desktop browser, **When** I open the staff area, **Then** I see a wide-screen layout with a navigation area for my role (receptionist, dentist, practice manager) that later features fill with their screens. 2. **Given** a phone, **When** a dentist opens "my day", **Then** the staff layout also fits without sideways scrolling (the dentist may use a phone). 3. **Given** a clinic day (08:00 to 20:00 IST, Monday to Saturday), **When** the reception screens are probed, **Then** availability over the month is reported against the 99.5% target. 4. **Given** a planned release during clinic hours, **When** it is deployed, **Then** the rolling replacement keeps reception screens available (no full outage). ---

items.title: The team sees problems before patients do
items.description_md: As the delivery team, we want structured logs without personal data, a health check, minute-by-minute availability probes, response-time measurement and alerts, so that we find and fix problems before the clinics notice and can prove the targets are met. **Why this priority**: The availability and speed targets are only real if they are measured; it also feeds the rollback triggers. **Independent Test**: Make a request and follow its correlation id through the logs; search all logs for a test patient's name, phone number and birth year and find none; stop the API in staging and confirm an alert arrives within the alert window. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the API is running, **When** `GET /health` is called, **Then** it reports whether the API and its database connection are working, and the interactive API documentation is reachable at `/docs`. 2. **Given** any request, **When** it is logged, **Then** the log carries ids and a correlation id and never contains a name, phone number or birth year; an automated test seeds personal data and fails if it appears in logs. 3. **Given** the production site, **When** a probe runs every minute reading the health check and the free-slot list, **Then** the result is recorded and monthly availability is calculated against 99.5%. 4. **Given** the free-slot list and booking confirmation, **When** requests are measured, **Then** 95% of free-slot requests finish within 2 s and 95% of booking confirmations within 3 s as seen by a phone on 4G, with server-side p95 at most 500 ms and 800 ms respectively. 5. **Given** a deploy, **When** health fails, 5xx exceeds 2% for 5 minutes, or reminder lag exceeds 15 minutes, **Then** the rollback alert fires; an alert also fires when reminder lag exceeds 10 minutes (Assumed: alerts go to the delivery team's shared channel, see open question Q3). 6. **Given** the monthly SLO report, **When** it is produced, **Then** it shows booking availability, reception-hours availability, slot and booking speed, reminders sent within 15 minutes (99%) and reminders sent for cancelled appointments (0). ---

user_story.i_want: structured logs without personal data, a health check, minute-by-minute availability probes, response-time measurement and alerts
user_story.so_that: we find and fix problems before the clinics notice and can prove the targets are met

items.title: Release 2 screens stay hidden until they are ready
items.description_md: As the practice manager, I want the Release 2 features (family members, no-show block, no-show report, reminders-failed list and SMS fallback) to be invisible to patients and staff until they are switched on, so that Release 1 goes live on 1 March 2027 without half-finished screens. **Why this priority**: Release 2 is about 2 to 3 weeks after go-live (due 2027-03-19); the switch must exist before any R2 work merges. **Independent Test**: Deploy a build with a sample R2 screen behind the switch. With the switch off it is not reachable or visible; with it on in staging it appears; switching it on in production needs no new deploy. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a Release 2 screen or action, **When** its switch is off, **Then** no menu entry, route or API action for it is visible or usable to patients or staff. 2. **Given** the switch for a feature is turned on in staging, **When** a user opens the app, **Then** the feature appears without a new deploy, and turning it off hides it again. 3. **Given** production at go-live, **When** the switch settings are reviewed, **Then** all Release 2 switches are off and the setting is recorded in the readiness checklist. 4. **Given** the switch is changed, **When** it is read, **Then** who changed it and when is recorded. ---

items.title: The service handles 100 concurrent users and a third clinic as data
items.description_md: As the practice manager, I want proof that the service copes with today's clinics, with 30 patients booking at once, and with a third clinic and 1,000 appointments a week, so that the business can grow without a rebuild. **Why this priority**: It proves NFR-003 before go-live and gives early warning if a design choice would block growth. **Independent Test**: Run the load test against staging sized like production with 100 concurrent simulated users (about 35 requests per second at peak) and the scale data set (3 clinics, 10 dentists, a year of appointments at 1,000 per week); read the results. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** staging sized like production and today's data (2 clinics, 6 dentists, about 450 appointments a week), **When** 30 simulated patients book at once, **Then** the free-slot and booking targets (2 s and 3 s for 95%) are met. 2. **Given** the same environment, **When** 100 concurrent simulated users run for at least 10 minutes at about 35 requests per second, **Then** the free-slot and booking targets are still met and there are no errors other than "slot taken". 3. **Given** a data set of 3 clinics, 10 dentists and 1,000 appointments a week for a year, **When** the load test runs again, **Then** the targets are still met with no change to the application code or the data structures. 4. **Given** a third clinic and a tenth dentist are added through the setup screens or data load, **When** patients open the site, **Then** they are offered without a deploy. 5. **Given** the load test results, **When** they are reviewed, **Then** they are recorded in the readiness checklist with the date and the environment size. ---

user_story.so_that: the business can grow without a rebuild

items.title: Release 1 is checked off as ready for UAT and go-live
items.description_md: As the practice manager, I want a go-live readiness checklist that the delivery team completes before the user acceptance test (UAT) and go-live, so that I can sign off by trying each flow and be confident Release 1 can go live on 1 March 2027. **Why this priority**: The date is firm (NFR-009); Release 1 must be UAT-ready by 2027-02-22. items.title: Patient signs in with a phone code
items.description_md: A returning patient opens the BrightSmile website on their phone, enters their phone number, receives a one-time code by SMS, enters it and is signed in. A wrong or expired code is reported clearly and the patient can ask for a new code. After 5 wrong tries the patient must wait 15 minutes before trying again. Once signed in, the patient stays signed in for 7 days from their last use so they do not need a new code for every visit. **Why this priority**: Every patient flow (booking, changing, cancelling) starts with signing in; without it nothing else in the product is reachable by patients. **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested with a test phone number and a stubbed message sender: request a code, enter it, and reach a signed-in state; then repeat with wrong, expired and repeated-wrong codes. Delivers a working patient sign-in. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient account exists for a phone number, **When** the patient enters the number and asks for a code, **Then** a 6-digit code is sent by SMS and the screen asks for the code. 2. **Given** a code was sent less than 10 minutes ago, **When** the patient enters it correctly, **Then** the patient is signed in and sees their own appointments area. 3. **Given** a code was sent, **When** the patient enters a wrong code, **Then** the screen says the code is wrong, shows how to get a new code, and the wrong try is counted. 4. **Given** a code was sent more than 10 minutes ago, **When** the patient enters it, **Then** the screen says the code has expired and offers a new code. 5. **Given** a patient has entered 5 wrong codes for a phone number, **When** they try again within 15 minutes (with the old or a new code), **Then** the system refuses and says to wait, and after 15 minutes a new code can be requested. 6. **Given** a patient has not used the site for less than 7 days, **When** they return, **Then** they are still signed in; **Given** 7 days without use, **Then** they must sign in again. 7. **Given** a single network address or a single day has produced too many code requests, **When** another code is requested, **Then** the request is refused without sending an SMS. ---

user_story.i_want: to sign in with my phone number and an SMS code, with clear messages for a wrong or expired code
user_story.so_that: I can reach my appointments without a password and stay signed in for 7 days, while my account is protected from guessing and code floods

items.title: New patient creates an account
items.description_md: A patient whose phone number is not yet known enters the number, verifies the code and is then asked for their name. Only after the code is verified and the name is given is the account created and the patient signed in. **Why this priority**: Most patients are new at go-live; without account creation they cannot book online. **Independent Test**: Use a phone number with no account: verify the code, give a name, and check that exactly one patient account and one person record exist and that no account exists if the code was never verified. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a phone number with no account, **When** the patient verifies a correct code, **Then** the screen asks for their name and no account exists yet. 2. **Given** the code is verified for a new number, **When** the patient gives a name, **Then** one account for that phone number and one person record with that name are created and the patient is signed in. 3. **Given** the code for a new number is wrong or expired, **When** the patient continues, **Then** no account is created. 4. **Given** the name is empty, **When** the patient submits, **Then** the screen asks for a name and creates nothing. 5. **Given** an account already exists for the phone number, **When** a patient signs in with it, **Then** no second account is created. ---

user_story.i_want: to verify my code, give my name and get an account created
user_story.so_that: I can book online without calling the clinic, and no account or personal data is stored for a number that never verified

items.title: Staff sign in with username and password
items.description_md: A receptionist, dentist or the practice manager opens the staff sign-in screen, enters their username and password and reaches the screen for their role. After 5 failed attempts for the same username the account is locked for 15 minutes. Staff sessions end after 8 hours, or after 30 minutes without use. Passwords are at least 10 characters long. **Why this priority**: Reception, dentists and the manager cannot run the clinic without signing in; it is also the first line of defence for patient data. **Independent Test**: Create a staff account in test data, sign in with right and wrong passwords, check lockout, idle and maximum session ends. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an active staff account, **When** the person enters the correct username and password, **Then** they are signed in and land on the screen for their role. 2. **Given** an active staff account, **When** a wrong password is entered, **Then** the screen says the username or password is wrong without saying which one. 3. **Given** 5 failed sign-ins for a username, **When** a sixth is tried within 15 minutes (even with the right password), **Then** it is refused with a message to wait; after 15 minutes sign-in works again. 4. **Given** a staff member is signed in, **When** 30 minutes pass without use or 8 hours pass since sign-in, **Then** the next request requires signing in again. 5. **Given** a password is set or changed, **When** it has fewer than 10 characters, **Then** it is rejected. 6. **Given** any screen or call, **When** it is reached over plain HTTP, **Then** it is not served; all traffic is over HTTPS. 7. **Given** a signed-in staff member, **When** they change their own password (giving the current one) or the manager sets a new password for them, **Then** the new password works at the next sign-in and the old one does not. ---

user_story.i_want: to sign in with my username and password and change my own password
user_story.so_that: I reach the screen for my role, and patient data is protected by lockout, session limits and a 10-character password minimum

items.title: Each role sees only what it needs
items.description_md: Whatever a person asks for, the system decides from who they are, not from ids they type or change. A patient sees only their own appointments and those of their family members. A receptionist sees and changes appointments of their own clinic only, but can search for any patient by phone number or name. A dentist sees only their own day and cannot change anything. The practice manager sees both clinics and the settings. Other features rely on this decision when they return data. **Why this priority**: This is the security core (role separation); every other module depends on it and a leak of patient data is the main product risk. **Independent Test**: Run an automated per-role test matrix: for each role and each protected operation, check allowed and refused results, including requests with another clinic's or patient's id. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient is signed in, **When** they ask for an appointment of a person who is not themselves or one of their family members, **Then** the system refuses it as if it did not exist. 2. **Given** a receptionist of clinic A, **When** they ask for or change an appointment of clinic B, **Then** the system refuses. 3. **Given** a receptionist of clinic A, **When** they search patients by phone number or name, **Then** they find patients regardless of clinic but see appointments of clinic A only. 4. **Given** a dentist is signed in, **When** they ask for another dentist's day or try to change anything, **Then** the system refuses. 5. **Given** the practice manager is signed in, **When** they open data of either clinic or the settings, **Then** it is allowed. 6. **Given** a person's role, clinic or active flag changed since they signed in, **When** they make their next request, **Then** the current values apply at once. 7. **Given** a request without sign-in, or one that changes data without coming from the BrightSmile website, **When** it is made, **Then** it is refused. ---

user_story.i_want: every request to be authorised on the server from the signed-in person's role, clinic and patient scope, never from ids in the request
user_story.so_that: receptionists, dentists and patients can reach only the data their role allows, with zero cross-clinic or cross-patient reads

items.title: Practice manager manages staff accounts
items.description_md: The practice manager opens the staff screen to create receptionist and dentist accounts, to assign each receptionist to a clinic, and to deactivate an account when a person leaves. A deactivated person cannot sign in, and a person already signed in loses access on their next request. **Why this priority**: Without staff accounts nobody can use reception or dentist screens; deactivation protects patient data when staff leave. **Independent Test**: As the manager, create a receptionist for Indiranagar, sign in as them, deactivate them, and confirm they cannot sign in and an open session stops working. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the manager is on the staff screen, **When** they create a receptionist with name, username, initial password and clinic, **Then** the account exists, is active and is assigned to that clinic. 2. **Given** the manager creates a dentist account, **When** it is saved, **Then** the dentist can sign in and see their own day. 3. **Given** a receptionist is assigned to one clinic, **When** the manager assigns them to another clinic, **Then** the receptionist's access follows the new clinic at once. 4. **Given** an active staff account, **When** the manager deactivates it, **Then** the person cannot sign in and an existing session is refused on its next request. 5. **Given** a username already exists, **When** the manager creates another with the same username, **Then** the system refuses. 6. **Given** a person who is not the practice manager, **When** they try to create, change or deactivate a staff account, **Then** the system refuses. 7. **Given** the manager is the only active manager, **When** they try to deactivate their own account, **Then** the system refuses. ---

items.title: Practice manager erases a patient's data on request
items.description_md: When a patient asks for their data to be deleted, the practice manager opens an admin screen, finds the patient account and starts erasure. The patient's name, phone number, family members' names and birth years, and stored messages are removed or anonymised within 30 days of the request. Appointment rows stay, anonymised, so clinic counts stay correct. **Why this priority**: Required by the DPDP Act and the privacy requirement, but not needed for the first sign-in flows; it must be ready by go-live. **Independent Test**: Create a patient with family members and appointments, run erasure, and check that no name, phone or birth year remains while appointment counts are unchanged. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the manager is on the erasure screen, **When** they find a patient account by phone number and confirm erasure, **Then** the request is recorded with its date and the account can no longer sign in. 2. **Given** an erasure was confirmed, **When** the process completes (within 30 days of the request), **Then** the account, the person records of the account holder and family members, and the stored messages hold no name, phone number or birth year. 3. **Given** the erased patient had appointments, **When** erasure completes, **Then** the appointment rows remain without any personal link. 4. **Given** the system stores personal data, **When** the stored fields are reviewed, **Then** only name, phone number, family members' names and birth years, appointments, treatment type and message choice are held; no clinical data. 5. **Given** a signed-in user who is not the practice manager, **When** they try to use erasure, **Then** it is refused. 6. **Given** logs are inspected, **When** any sign-in or erasure activity is searched, **Then** no name, phone number or birth year appears. 7. **Given** sign-in codes and old personal data exist, **When** retention periods pass (sign-in codes 24 hours, accounts idle for 24 months, staff 24 months after deactivation), **Then** they are deleted or anonymised; messages (90 days) and appointments (24 months) follow the same rule in the features that own them. ---

user_story.i_want: to erase a patient's personal data on request within 30 days and have old sign-in codes and idle accounts purged on schedule
user_story.so_that: BrightSmile complies with the DPDP Act while appointment counts stay correct

items.title: Clinics and dentists held as data
items.description_md: The practice manager keeps the list of clinics (name, address, phone) and the list of dentists in the staff screens. Today there are 2 clinics (Indiranagar and Whitefield) and 6 dentists. When a third clinic opens, the manager adds it in the same screen; it is then offered to patients and reception with no code change and no deploy. A clinic or a dentist that is no longer in use is marked inactive, not deleted. Every appointment belongs to exactly one clinic and exactly one dentist, so the other features can only pick from active clinics and dentists that this list holds. **Why this priority**: Every other part of the system (hours, slots, bookings, day view) hangs on clinics and dentists existing as data. Without it nothing can be set up. **Independent Test**: As the practice manager, add a third clinic and a new dentist in the staff screens. Both appear in the lists returned to patient and reception screens straight away, with no restart or deploy. Mark the clinic inactive and see it disappear from the lists offered for new bookings. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the practice manager is signed in and 2 active clinics exist, **When** they add a clinic with a name, address and phone number, **Then** the clinic is saved as active and appears in the clinic list for all roles without any deploy. 2. **Given** a dentist exists, **When** the manager edits the dentist's name or marks the dentist inactive, **Then** the change is saved and an inactive dentist is no longer offered for new bookings. 3. **Given** a clinic or dentist that has appointments, **When** the manager marks it inactive, **Then** existing appointments are kept unchanged and the record is not deleted. 4. **Given** a signed-in receptionist, dentist or patient, **When** they try to add, edit or deactivate a clinic or a dentist, **Then** the system refuses and nothing changes. 5. **Given** a clinic name already in use by an active clinic, **When** the manager saves a second clinic with the same name, **Then** the system refuses it and says why. ---

user_story.i_want: to add, edit and deactivate clinics and dentists in the staff screens
user_story.so_that: a third clinic can open and be offered to patients and reception with no code change and no deploy

items.title: Treatment types with duration and online flag
items.description_md: The system holds the list of treatment types, each with a name, a duration in minutes and a flag saying whether patients may book it online. The online types are check-up, cleaning and consultation, 30 minutes each. Other types (for example root canal and extraction) are 60 or 90 minutes and are booked by reception only. The practice manager adds, edits and deactivates types in a "Treatments" screen. Patients see only active online types; reception sees all active types. **Why this priority**: The duration of a treatment decides how long a free slot must be, and the online flag decides what patients may book. Booking and slot search cannot work without it. **Independent Test**: As the manager, add "Root canal" with 90 minutes and online off, and change "Check-up" to 30 minutes online on. Ask for the list as a patient (only active online types) and as reception (all active types) and check both. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the system is set up, **When** any signed-in user asks for the treatment list, **Then** check-up, cleaning and consultation are present as online types of 30 minutes each. 2. **Given** the manager is signed in, **When** they add a treatment type with a name, a duration and the online flag off, **Then** the type is saved and is visible to reception but not to patients. 3. **Given** a treatment type, **When** the manager changes its duration or online flag, **Then** the change applies to slots and bookings made from then on and does not change existing appointments. 4. **Given** a treatment type, **When** the manager marks it inactive, **Then** it is no longer offered for new bookings and existing appointments keep it. 5. **Given** a duration that is not a positive multiple of 30 minutes, **When** the manager saves a treatment type, **Then** the system refuses it and says why. 6. **Given** a signed-in receptionist, dentist or patient, **When** they try to add or edit a treatment type, **Then** the system refuses it. ---

user_story.i_want: to maintain treatment types with a duration and an online flag
user_story.so_that: patients can book only suitable treatments online and every slot is as long as the treatment needs

items.title: Weekly working hours and breaks per dentist per clinic
items.description_md: The practice manager sets, for each dentist and each clinic the dentist works at, the weekly working hours: for each weekday, a start and an end, plus any breaks (for example lunch). A dentist can work at more than one clinic on set days, for example Monday to Wednesday at Indiranagar and Thursday to Saturday at Whitefield. The manager opens the "Dentists and hours" screen, picks a dentist and a clinic, and edits the week. **Why this priority**: Working hours minus breaks are the raw material for free slots. No hours means no slots, so no online booking. **Independent Test**: As the manager, give a dentist Monday 09:00–17:00 with a 13:00–14:00 break at Indiranagar and Thursday 10:00–18:00 at Whitefield. Reading the week back shows exactly this. Try to give the same dentist overlapping hours at the other clinic on Monday and see it refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist and a clinic, **When** the manager sets Monday 09:00–17:00 with a break 13:00–14:00, **Then** the hours and the break are saved and shown again when the week is opened. 2. **Given** a dentist who works Monday at clinic A, **When** the manager adds Thursday hours at clinic B, **Then** both are kept and the dentist is shown as working at both clinics on those days. 3. **Given** a dentist with hours at clinic A on Monday 09:00–17:00, **When** the manager saves Monday 15:00–19:00 for the same dentist at clinic B, **Then** the system refuses it because the dentist cannot be at two clinics at the same time. 4. **Given** a weekday's hours, **When** the manager enters an end that is not after the start, a break outside the hours, or two overlapping breaks, **Then** the system refuses it and names the problem. 5. **Given** a dentist with weekly hours, **When** the manager removes a weekday's hours (a day off), **Then** that weekday no longer produces free slots for that dentist at that clinic. 6. **Given** a signed-in receptionist, dentist or patient, **When** they try to change weekly hours, **Then** the system refuses it. A receptionist or dentist may read hours. 7. **Given** appointments already booked outside newly changed hours, **When** the manager saves the change, **Then** the hours are saved and the system does not move or cancel those appointments. ---

user_story.i_want: to set each dentist's weekly working hours and breaks at each clinic
user_story.so_that: free slots match when dentists really work, including dentists who split the week between two clinics

items.title: Free slots for a clinic, dentist and treatment
items.description_md: For one clinic and one date range, the system works out each dentist's free slots: the dentist's working hours at that clinic, minus breaks, minus leave, minus appointments that are already booked (at any clinic, because a dentist cannot be in two places). Slots start on the hour or half hour and are as long as the chosen treatment. The system can also give "first available": the earliest free slots across all of that clinic's dentists, 10 at a time, with further pages on request. A patient only sees online treatment types and slots inside the booking horizon (today and the 30 days after; the number of days is a setting); reception can search any active type. Slots are shown in India time. **Why this priority**: The booking features (online and reception) are built on this calculation. It also carries the speed target: free slots must show within 2 seconds for 95% of requests on a 4G phone. **Independent Test**: With a dentist's Monday 09:00–17:00, break 13:00–14:00, leave 15:00–16:00 and a booked 10:00–10:30 appointment, ask for Monday's 30-minute slots and check that exactly the expected start times come back. Ask for a 90-minute treatment and check that every returned slot fits fully inside free time. Ask for "first available" and check the first page has 10 slots in time order and the next page continues. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist working Monday 09:00–17:00 at a clinic with a break 13:00–14:00, **When** free 30-minute slots are requested for that Monday, **Then** slots start at 09:00, 09:30 and so on on the hour or half hour, none start in 13:00–13:59, and the last one starts at 16:30. 2. **Given** the same dentist with an appointment booked 10:00–10:30, **When** slots are requested, **Then** the 10:00 slot is not offered and 10:30 is. 3. **Given** the same dentist is booked at another clinic on that Monday at 11:00–11:30, **When** slots are requested for this clinic, **Then** the 11:00 slot is not offered. 4. **Given** leave recorded for that dentist from 15:00 to 16:00 on that Monday, **When** slots are requested, **Then** no slot overlaps 15:00–16:00. 5. **Given** a 90-minute treatment, **When** slots are requested, **Then** a slot is offered only if the whole 90 minutes fit in working time without touching a break, leave or booked appointment. 6. **Given** a signed-in patient, **When** they ask for slots, **Then** only online treatment types are accepted, only slots from now up to the end of the booking horizon are returned, and only active clinics and dentists are included. 7. **Given** a clinic with several dentists, **When** "first available" is requested, **Then** the 10 earliest free slots across the clinic's dentists are returned in time order, each with its dentist, and asking for the next page returns the following 10. 8. **Given** a date range with no free slot, **When** slots are requested, **Then** an empty list is returned (not an error). 9. **Given** a request for slots at a clinic or dentist that is inactive, or a treatment type that is inactive, **When** it is made, **Then** no slots are returned. 10. **Given** a booking made by another part of the system just before the request, **When** slots are requested, **Then** that appointment is already excluded. ---

user_story.i_want: to see the free slots for a clinic, dentist and treatment, and the first available times
user_story.so_that: I can pick a time that is really free, and see it within 2 seconds

items.title: Record dentist leave
items.description_md: The practice manager records a dentist's leave, either for whole days (from a first day to a last day) or for part of a day (a day with a start time and an end time). Leave applies to the dentist at every clinic. As soon as leave is saved, the system shows the manager the appointments already booked in that time, so reception can move them. The system never moves or cancels them by itself. Leave removes free slots for that dentist at once. A leave entry entered by mistake can be deleted. **Why this priority**: Needed before go-live so absences do not leave patients booked with a dentist who is away, but the first bookings can be made before any leave exists. **Independent Test**: As the manager, record a whole-day leave on a day when the dentist has 3 booked appointments (using the in-process appointment stand-in until the booking feature exists). The answer lists those 3 appointments, none is changed, and free slots for that day are empty. Record a part-day leave and check only overlapping appointments are listed. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist, **When** the manager records leave for whole days from a first day to a last day, **Then** the leave is saved from the start of the first day to the end of the last day in India time. 2. **Given** a dentist, **When** the manager records part-day leave with a date, a start time and an end time, **Then** the leave is saved for exactly that time. 3. **Given** booked appointments that overlap the new leave, **When** the leave is saved, **Then** the response and screen list each of those appointments (date, time, clinic, patient name, phone number, treatment) and the system does not change any of them. 4. **Given** an appointment that only partly overlaps the leave, **When** the leave is saved, **Then** that appointment is listed too. 5. **Given** cancelled appointments or appointments outside the leave time, **When** the leave is saved, **Then** they are not listed. 6. **Given** saved leave, **When** free slots are requested for those days, **Then** no slot overlaps the leave. 7. **Given** a leave end that is not after its start, or a leave that has already ended, **When** the manager saves it, **Then** the system refuses it and says why. 8. **Given** leave entered by mistake, **When** the manager deletes it, **Then** slots in that time come back and the appointments are no longer on any to-move list because of it. 9. **Given** a signed-in receptionist, dentist or patient, **When** they try to record or delete leave, **Then** the system refuses it. ---

user_story.i_want: to record a dentist's whole-day or part-day leave and see the appointments that overlap it
user_story.so_that: patients are not left booked with an absent dentist and reception can move them

items.title: Reception sees the appointments to move
items.description_md: Reception opens a "To move" list for their own clinic. It shows the booked appointments that fall inside a dentist's leave at that clinic, earliest first, so the receptionist can phone the patient and move the visit. The list updates by itself: an appointment disappears from it once it has been moved or cancelled. A receptionist never sees another clinic's list; the practice manager can see the list of any clinic. This feature only lists; moving an appointment is done in the reception features. **Why this priority**: It is how a leave becomes action. It depends on leave (User Story 5) and on appointments from the booking feature, so it follows them. **Independent Test**: With leave covering two appointments at Indiranagar and one at Whitefield, sign in as an Indiranagar receptionist and check only the two Indiranagar appointments appear. Cancel one of them (through the booking stand-in) and check it drops off the list. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** leave that covers booked appointments at the receptionist's clinic, **When** the receptionist opens the to-move list, **Then** those appointments are listed with date, time, dentist, patient name, phone number and treatment, earliest first. 2. **Given** leave that also covers appointments at another clinic, **When** the receptionist asks for the list, **Then** only their own clinic's appointments are returned, and asking for another clinic is refused. 3. **Given** an appointment on the list, **When** it is moved to a time outside the leave or cancelled, **Then** it no longer appears on the next read. 4. **Given** nothing to move, **When** the list is opened, **Then** it says there is nothing to move. 5. **Given** the practice manager is signed in, **When** they ask for the to-move list of any clinic, **Then** it is returned. 6. **Given** a patient or dentist role, **When** they ask for the to-move list, **Then** the system refuses it. ---

items.title: Patient online booking
items.description_md: Patient books a slot online (clinic, treatment, dentist or first available), never double-booked, with channel choice remembered.

items.title: Book a free slot online
items.description_md: A signed-in patient opens the booking flow on a phone, chooses who the visit is for (themselves; family members arrive with feature 008), the clinic and one of the online treatment types (check-up, cleaning or consultation, 30 minutes each). They then choose a dentist at that clinic or "first available", pick a day within the next 30 days and a free slot, confirm, and see the booked appointment. "First available" shows the earliest free slots across all of that clinic's dentists. The system records the booking and asks for the confirmation message to be sent. **Why this priority**: This is the reason for the project: patients book without phoning in clinic hours. Without it nothing else in the feature has value. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a test patient, book a check-up at a clinic with a named dentist, then book a cleaning with "first available". Both appear as booked appointments in the right clinic, with the right dentist, start and end time, and a confirmation request is recorded for each. Delivering this story alone (with SMS as the only channel) is a viable MVP slice. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient on the first booking screen, **When** they choose themselves, a clinic and "check-up", **Then** they can continue to the dentist and slot step, and only the online treatment types (check-up, cleaning, consultation) are offered. 2. **Given** a clinic with several dentists working in the next 30 days, **When** the patient chooses "first available", **Then** the earliest free slots across all that clinic's dentists are shown, each with its dentist and time, soonest first. 3. **Given** a patient who chose a named dentist, **When** they open the day picker, **Then** only days from today to 30 days after today are offered (1 March shows up to 31 March), and the free slots of that dentist for the chosen day are listed, each on the hour or half hour. 4. **Given** a patient on the confirm screen with a free slot, **When** they confirm, **Then** one appointment is created with status "booked" for that patient, clinic, dentist, treatment, start and end, and the booked screen shows clinic, dentist, treatment, date and time in India time. 5. **Given** a confirmed booking, **When** it is saved, **Then** a request to send the booking confirmation in the patient's chosen channel is recorded together with the booking (so it cannot be lost) for the confirmation feature, and the patient's screen does not wait for the message to be delivered. 6. **Given** a patient who is not signed in, **When** they try to open or submit any booking step, **Then** they are sent to sign-in and nothing is booked. 7. **Given** a patient who asks to book a treatment that patients cannot book online (for example a root canal), **When** the request reaches the system, **Then** it is refused with a clear message to phone the clinic, and nothing is booked. 8. **Given** a patient for whom the repeat no-show check (feature 009) says "blocked", **When** they start to book, **Then** the page says online booking is not available and shows the clinic's phone number. Until feature 009 exists the check always says "not blocked". 9. **Given** a new patient who has just signed in, **When** they book, **Then** they reach the booked screen in 5 screens or fewer, every tap target is at least 44 px, and no screen needs sideways scrolling on a phone. ---

items.title: A slot is never booked twice
items.description_md: If another booking takes the slot while the patient is choosing, the patient is told the slot has just been taken and is shown the next free slots, so they can pick another without starting again. If the patient's confirm request is repeated (a double tap or a network retry), only one appointment is made. **Why this priority**: A double-booked dentist is the worst failure for a clinic; the clinic must be able to trust the online diary. **Independent Test**: Start two bookings for the same dentist and slot, confirm both. Exactly one succeeds; the other is told "slot taken" and is shown the next free slots. Repeat the same confirm request twice and see one appointment. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** two patients who both chose the same dentist and slot, **When** both confirm at nearly the same time, **Then** exactly one booking is made and the other patient is told the slot was just taken. 2. **Given** a patient told the slot is taken, **When** the message is shown, **Then** it comes with the next free slots (same clinic, treatment and dentist choice as before) and the patient can choose one and confirm without re-entering clinic or treatment. 3. **Given** a patient who confirms and the screen does not respond, **When** the same confirm request is sent again with the same request key, **Then** the system returns the original booking and does not create a second appointment. 4. **Given** a slot that is already booked, **When** a booking for it arrives by any route, **Then** it is never saved as a second active appointment for that dentist. 5. **Given** a dentist who already has an active appointment (including a longer one made by reception), **When** a booking is requested whose time overlaps it even in part, **Then** it is refused as "slot taken". 6. **Given** a patient who is told "slot taken" and there are no further free slots in the next 30 days for their choice, **When** the answer is shown, **Then** the patient is told no slots are free and offered the clinic's phone number. ---

user_story.so_that: I never get a double or duplicate booking and can pick another time without starting again

items.title: Choose SMS or WhatsApp, remembered for next time
items.description_md: On the confirm screen the patient chooses SMS or WhatsApp for messages about this appointment. The first time the choice is SMS. When they confirm, the choice is saved with the appointment and remembered as their choice for their next booking. **Why this priority**: The confirmation and reminder messages depend on the channel; it is part of the booking and costs the patient one tap. **Independent Test**: A new patient sees SMS selected on the confirm screen. They choose WhatsApp and confirm; the appointment holds WhatsApp. On the next booking, WhatsApp is already selected. They switch to SMS for that booking; the next booking after that starts on SMS. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient who has never booked online, **When** the confirm screen opens, **Then** SMS is selected. 2. **Given** a patient who selects WhatsApp and confirms, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the appointment holds channel WhatsApp and the patient's remembered choice becomes WhatsApp. 3. **Given** a patient whose remembered choice is WhatsApp, **When** they start another booking, **Then** the confirm screen starts with WhatsApp selected and they can change it. 4. **Given** a booking that fails because the slot was taken, **When** the patient is shown other slots, **Then** their channel choice on screen is kept, and the remembered choice changes only when a booking is confirmed. 5. **Given** a channel value other than SMS or WhatsApp in a request, **When** it is submitted, **Then** it is refused and nothing is booked. ---

items.title: Prove that concurrent bookings never overlap
items.description_md: The delivery team can run a repeatable test that makes many patients try to book the same dentist and slot at once and checks the diary afterwards. It shows that no dentist ever has two overlapping active appointments. **Why this priority**: This is a main design risk of the system (quality scenario QA-003). It must be proven before go-live, but patients do not see it, so it follows the booking stories. **Independent Test**: Run the concurrency test suite against a staging-like database: 1,000 runs, each with many simultaneous attempts on one dentist and slot, with some attempts overlapping a neighbouring slot. Every run ends with 0 overlapping active appointments and exactly one winner per contested slot. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a free slot and 30 simultaneous booking attempts for it, **When** all complete, **Then** exactly one is booked, 29 are told "slot taken", and 0 overlapping active appointments exist for that dentist. 2. **Given** 1,000 concurrent-attempt runs, **When** the suite finishes, **Then** 0 overlapping active appointments for one dentist are found in 100% of the runs. 3. **Given** a run that includes up to 100 simultaneous attempts (the design load), **When** it finishes, **Then** the same result holds. 4. **Given** repeated attempts that carry the same request key, **When** the run finishes, **Then** they produce one appointment each, not more. 5. **Given** the test is part of the delivery pipeline, **When** it fails, **Then** the release is stopped. ---

items.title: Booking is quick on a phone network
items.description_md: On a 4G phone, free slots appear within 2 seconds and a confirmed booking within 3 seconds, for 95% of requests. The delivery team can run a performance check that shows this at the expected load. **Why this priority**: Patients give up on slow screens; the targets are our proposals (open for confirmation at the client gate), so they must be measured rather than assumed. **Independent Test**: Run the performance check with 100 simulated concurrent patients (about 35 requests a second) browsing slots and booking. Report the 95th percentile of slot list and booking times, on the server and as measured from a 4G-like client. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** 100 concurrent simulated patients, **When** they open the slot picker, **Then** 95% of slot lists are shown within 2 seconds on a 4G-like connection, and the server answers 95% within 500 ms. 2. **Given** the same load, **When** patients confirm bookings, **Then** 95% of confirmations are shown within 3 seconds on a 4G-like connection, and the server answers 95% within 800 ms. 3. **Given** a booking is confirmed, **When** the request is timed, **Then** the time to send the confirmation message is not part of it (the message is sent after the booking is saved). 4. **Given** the check runs on a pull request or before release, **When** a target is missed, **Then** the report names which target and the release owner sees it. 5. **Given** a "first available" request across all dentists of a clinic, **When** it is timed, **Then** it also meets the 2 second target. ---

items.title: See my upcoming and past appointments
items.description_md: A signed-in patient opens "My appointments" and sees every upcoming appointment and every past appointment, each with clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time (IST) and its status (booked, arrived, no-show, cancelled by the patient, cancelled by the clinic). The list is built per account, so when family members exist (feature 008, Release 2) their appointments appear for the account holder, each naming the person it is for. Opening one appointment shows its detail screen with the buttons or the phone number described in the cancel and reschedule stories. **Why this priority**: Every other action starts from this list; patients cannot manage a visit they cannot find. Must for the 1 March 2027 MVP. **Independent Test**: Seed an account with upcoming, past, cancelled and no-show appointments (and a second person on the same account); sign in and open "My appointments". Delivers value alone: a patient can check their visits and statuses without phoning. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient with two upcoming and three past appointments, **When** they open "My appointments", **Then** the upcoming ones are listed soonest first and the past ones most recent first, each with clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time in IST and status. 2. **Given** an account that also holds appointments for another person on the same account, **When** the account holder opens the list, **Then** those appointments appear too and each shows the name of the person it is for. 3. **Given** another patient's appointment exists, **When** the signed-in patient requests the list or opens that appointment by its identifier, **Then** it is not shown and the request is refused as not found. 4. **Given** a patient with no appointments, **When** they open the list, **Then** a plain message says there are none and offers "Book". 5. **Given** an appointment cancelled by the clinic, **When** the patient views the list, **Then** it appears in the past/cancelled part with the status "cancelled by the clinic". ---

user_story.so_that: I can check my visits and open one to manage it without phoning the clinic

items.title: Every status change records who and when
items.description_md: Each appointment has a status: booked, arrived, no-show, cancelled by the patient or cancelled by the clinic. Every change of status, and every reschedule, writes a history entry with the old and new status, who made it (the patient, or a named staff member), when, and a reason. Cancels or moves made at reception (feature 006) use the same recording: a reception cancel is recorded as "cancelled by the patient" when the patient asked, otherwise "cancelled by the clinic". Only the five statuses are accepted. **Why this priority**: Without it a patient can deny "I never cancelled" and the cancel and reschedule stories cannot be trusted; it is built first so they can use it. **Independent Test**: Through the shared status operation, cancel as the patient, cancel by reception (patient asked and not asked) and mark arrived and no-show; read the history of each appointment and check actor, time, from and to status, reason; try an invalid status and see it refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment, **When** the patient cancels it, **Then** a history entry exists with from status "booked", to status "cancelled by the patient", the patient as actor, the time of the change and the reason "patient request". 2. **Given** a booked appointment, **When** a patient reschedules it, **Then** a history entry records the old and new time and dentist, with status booked before and after, the patient as actor and the time. 3. **Given** a receptionist cancels at a patient's request, **When** the change is saved through the shared status operation, **Then** the new status is "cancelled by the patient" and the actor is the receptionist; when the clinic itself cancels it is "cancelled by the clinic". 4. **Given** any code path tries to write a status outside the five allowed values, **When** it is saved, **Then** the data store refuses it. 5. **Given** a status change fails, **When** the transaction ends, **Then** neither the new status nor a history entry is stored (both or neither). 6. **Given** history older than 24 months, **When** the retention job runs, **Then** history is removed on the same schedule as its appointment's personal link. ---

items.title: Cancel an upcoming appointment
items.description_md: From the appointment screen a patient taps "Cancel", confirms, and sees a "done" screen. The slot is free for other patients at once and the patient gets a message in their chosen channel. Less than 4 hours before the start, the Cancel and Change time buttons are replaced by the clinic's phone number. **Why this priority**: Frees chairs for other patients, which supports the goal of fewer empty slots; firm MVP. **Independent Test**: Cancel one booked appointment more than 4 hours ahead and one less than 4 hours ahead (clock controlled in test). The first becomes cancelled by the patient, its slot is bookable, a message is queued; the second shows the phone number and the cancel request is refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment starting in more than 4 hours, **When** the patient taps "Cancel" and confirms, **Then** the status becomes "cancelled by the patient", the done screen is shown, and the slot appears again in the free slots straight away. 2. **Given** a successful cancel, **When** it is saved, **Then** the patient receives a cancellation message in the channel chosen for that appointment, and no reminder is sent for it. 3. **Given** a booked appointment starting in less than 4 hours, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** no Cancel or Change time button is shown and the clinic's phone number is shown instead. 4. **Given** the patient kept the screen open past the cut-off, **When** they confirm a cancel less than 4 hours before the start, **Then** the request is refused, nothing changes, and the clinic's phone number is shown. 5. **Given** an appointment that is already cancelled, arrived or no-show, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** no Cancel or Change time button is shown. 6. **Given** the patient taps Cancel twice, or sends the request again after a slow network, **When** the second request arrives, **Then** the appointment is cancelled once, one message is created and the patient sees the same result. ---

items.title: Reschedule an upcoming appointment
items.description_md: A patient taps "Change time" on an upcoming appointment, sees free slots at the same clinic for the same treatment with any dentist, picks one and confirms. The appointment moves to the new slot, the old slot is free at once, and the patient gets a message in their chosen channel. Not allowed less than 4 hours before the original start. A patient who is blocked by the repeat no-show rule (feature 009, Release 2) cannot reschedule online; until that feature exists the block check always answers "not blocked". **Why this priority**: Rescheduling keeps the visit rather than losing it; firm MVP. **Independent Test**: Reschedule a booked appointment to another dentist's free slot at the same clinic; verify one appointment holds the new slot, the old slot is free, a history row exists and a message is queued. Repeat with the slot taken meanwhile and with the policy answering "blocked". **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment starting in more than 4 hours, **When** the patient taps "Change time", **Then** the slot picker shows free slots at the same clinic for the same treatment, for any dentist working there, and no other clinic or treatment. 2. **Given** the patient picks a free slot and confirms, **When** the change is saved, **Then** the same appointment now has the new time and dentist, its status stays "booked", the done screen shows the new details, and the old slot is bookable at once. 3. **Given** a successful reschedule, **When** it is saved, **Then** the patient receives a message in the chosen channel with the new details, the reminder for the old time is withdrawn and a reminder exists for the new time only (by feature 007). 4. **Given** two people confirm the same slot at once, **When** the second confirm arrives, **Then** it is refused with a "slot just taken" answer, the patient's original appointment is untouched, and the next free slots are shown. 5. **Given** an appointment starting in less than 4 hours, **When** the patient asks to reschedule, **Then** the request is refused and the clinic's phone number is shown. 6. **Given** the no-show policy answers "blocked" for this patient, **When** they try to reschedule, **Then** the request is refused with a message to phone the clinic, and their existing booking stays booked. 7. **Given** the reschedule cannot be completed (for example the message cannot be created), **When** the error occurs, **Then** the appointment stays at its old time and nothing is half-saved. 8. **Given** the patient picks the slot they already hold, **When** they confirm, **Then** nothing changes and the patient is told it is the same time. ---

items.title: Open my appointment from the message link
items.description_md: A patient taps the link in a confirmation or reminder message. If not signed in they sign in with the phone code, then land on that appointment's screen. They can only open it if it belongs to their account; the link carries no authority by itself. **Why this priority**: Most patients will arrive from a message, but "My appointments" already covers the same actions, so this follows the P1 stories. **Independent Test**: Open the link signed out, sign in as the owner and land on the appointment; repeat as a different patient and get "not found". **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-out patient opens an appointment link, **When** they finish sign-in, **Then** they are taken to that appointment and not to the home page. 2. **Given** a signed-in patient opens a link to an appointment on their account, **When** the page loads, **Then** the appointment screen shows with the buttons or phone number that apply. 3. **Given** a signed-in patient opens a link to an appointment on another account, **When** the page loads, **Then** nothing about it is shown and the answer is "not found". 4. **Given** a link for an appointment that is cancelled or in the past, **When** the owner opens it, **Then** the appointment is shown read only with its status. ---

items.title: Reception day view, check-in, no-show and dentist day
items.description_md: Reception day view per clinic, book/move/cancel for callers and walk-ins, arrived, no-show and undo; dentist read-only day.

items.title: See the day of my clinic
items.description_md: A receptionist signs in and sees today's day view for their own clinic: one column per dentist working that day, each appointment showing patient name, phone number, treatment and status. They can move to other days. Opening an appointment shows the appointment panel with the actions that apply. **Why this priority**: It replaces the paper diary and is the screen every other reception action starts from. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a receptionist of clinic A with seeded dentists and appointments at clinics A and B. The day view shows only clinic A, one column per dentist working that day, and the day can be changed forward and back. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a receptionist of clinic A and three dentists with working hours at clinic A today, **When** they sign in, **Then** they see today's date (IST) with three columns, one per dentist, each listing that dentist's appointments in time order with patient name, phone number, treatment and status. 2. **Given** a dentist who works at both clinics today, **When** the receptionist of clinic A opens the day view, **Then** the column shows only that dentist's appointments at clinic A. 3. **Given** the day view for today, **When** the receptionist chooses next day, previous day or picks a date, **Then** the view shows that date's columns and appointments for their clinic. 4. **Given** a date on which no dentist works at the clinic and no appointment exists (for example a Sunday), **When** the receptionist opens it, **Then** the view says no dentists are working that day. 5. **Given** the day view is open, **When** another receptionist books or changes an appointment, **Then** the change appears within about 30 seconds without the receptionist reloading. 6. **Given** an appointment in the view, **When** the receptionist selects it, **Then** an appointment panel opens with the details and only the actions that apply to its current status and time. ---

user_story.i_want: to see today's day view of my clinic with one column per dentist and move to other days
user_story.so_that: I can run the day from one screen instead of the paper diary

(source: FR-019)

items.title: Mark a patient as arrived
items.description_md: When a patient arrives, the receptionist marks the appointment as arrived and the column shows the new status. **Why this priority**: Check-in is the most frequent action during the day and feeds the no-show numbers. **Independent Test**: Open a booked appointment of today, mark it arrived, and see the status change and the recorded actor and time. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment today at the receptionist's clinic, **When** the receptionist marks it arrived, **Then** its status becomes arrived in the day view and the change records the receptionist and the time. 2. **Given** an appointment on a future date, **When** the receptionist opens its panel, **Then** "Arrived" is not offered. 3. **Given** an appointment already changed by another receptionist (for example cancelled), **When** the receptionist tries to mark it arrived, **Then** the system refuses, says the appointment's current status and refreshes the view. 4. **Given** an appointment of the other clinic, **When** the receptionist tries to mark it arrived by any means, **Then** the system refuses and nothing changes. ---

user_story.so_that: the day view shows who is here and the check-in is recorded with who and when

items.title: Mark a no-show and undo it the same day
items.description_md: When a patient has not come 15 minutes after the start time, the receptionist marks a no-show. The mark can be set from 15 minutes after the start until the end of that day, and undone the same day. **Why this priority**: No-shows are the clinic's biggest problem; the status must be recorded reliably and fixable. **Independent Test**: With an appointment that started 20 minutes ago, mark no-show, then undo; also try at 10 minutes after the start and on the next day. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment that started 15 minutes ago or more today, **When** the receptionist marks it a no-show, **Then** the status becomes no-show and the change records who and when. 2. **Given** a booked appointment that started less than 15 minutes ago, **When** the receptionist opens its panel, **Then** "No-show" is not offered and an attempt through the system is refused with the time from which it is allowed. 3. **Given** an appointment marked no-show today, **When** the receptionist chooses undo on the same day, **Then** the status returns to booked and the undo records who and when. 4. **Given** an appointment of a day that has ended (after midnight IST), **When** the receptionist tries to mark a no-show or undo one, **Then** the system refuses. 5. **Given** an appointment with status arrived, cancelled by the patient or cancelled by the clinic, **When** the receptionist tries to mark it a no-show, **Then** the system refuses. ---

user_story.i_want: to mark a no-show from 15 minutes after the start and undo it the same day
user_story.so_that: no-shows are recorded reliably and mistakes can be fixed

Given an appointment marked no-show today, When the receptionist chooses undo on the same day, Then the status returns to booked and the undo records who and when. (source: FR-022)

items.title: Find or create a patient
items.description_md: A patient phones or walks in. The receptionist finds the patient by phone number or name, or creates one with name and phone number. **Why this priority**: Every reception-side booking starts from a patient. **Independent Test**: Search by a phone number and by a name; create a patient with a new phone number; try to create with an existing phone number. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** existing patients, **When** the receptionist searches by part of a phone number or name, **Then** matching patients are listed with name and phone number only. 2. **Given** a patient who has appointments only at the other clinic, **When** the receptionist searches for them, **Then** the patient is found, but no appointment of the other clinic is shown. 3. **Given** no match, **When** the receptionist enters a name and a phone number, **Then** a new patient is created and selected for booking. 4. **Given** a phone number that already has an account, **When** the receptionist tries to create a patient with it, **Then** the system offers the existing patient instead of creating a duplicate. 5. **Given** a missing name or a phone number that is not valid, **When** the receptionist saves, **Then** the system says what to correct and creates nothing. ---

items.title: Book a patient, including long treatments and walk-ins
items.description_md: For a selected patient the receptionist books any treatment type, including reception-only types of 60 or 90 minutes, into a free slot of their clinic, with no 4-hour cut-off. A walk-in is booked as a normal appointment and marked arrived. **Why this priority**: Phone and walk-in booking is how reception works today, and longer treatments can only be booked here. It is also how the paper diary is typed in before go-live. **Independent Test**: Book a 90-minute treatment for tomorrow and a 30-minute walk-in for the next free slot today; verify both appear in the day view, and that two receptionists booking the same slot cannot both succeed. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a selected patient, **When** the receptionist chooses a reception-only treatment type (60 or 90 minutes), a dentist and a free slot long enough, **Then** the appointment is booked at the receptionist's clinic and appears in the dentist's column. 2. **Given** a free slot that starts in 2 hours, **When** the receptionist books it, **Then** it is booked, because there is no 4-hour cut-off for reception. 3. **Given** a patient who is present and not booked, **When** the receptionist books a free slot as a walk-in, **Then** the appointment is created as a normal appointment and its status is arrived. 4. **Given** two receptionists confirm the same slot at once, **When** both submit, **Then** one booking succeeds and the other is told the slot is taken and sees the next free slots. 5. **Given** a free slot on a date more than 30 days ahead, **When** the receptionist books it, **Then** the booking is accepted (the 30-day limit applies to online booking only), which also allows typing in the paper diary before go-live. 6. **Given** a slot that is not free (break, leave, existing appointment, or too short for the treatment), **When** the receptionist looks for slots, **Then** it is not offered. ---

user_story.so_that: phone and walk-in patients are booked without double bookings and the paper diary can be typed in before go-live

items.title: Reschedule or cancel for a patient
items.description_md: The receptionist moves an appointment of their clinic to another free slot, or cancels it, at any time before it starts or later the same day, with no 4-hour cut-off. A cancel records whether the patient asked or the clinic did. **Why this priority**: Callers change plans by phone; reception must be able to do it, but it builds on the booking and day view. **Independent Test**: Move a booked appointment to another dentist's free slot; cancel one as "patient asked" and one as "clinic"; check statuses and that the slots become free. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment at the receptionist's clinic, **When** they pick another free slot (same clinic, any dentist) and confirm, **Then** the appointment moves, the old slot is free at once, and the change records who and when. 2. **Given** an appointment starting in 1 hour, **When** the receptionist reschedules or cancels it, **Then** it is allowed. 3. **Given** a cancel, **When** the receptionist states that the patient asked, **Then** the status becomes cancelled by the patient. 4. **Given** a cancel, **When** the receptionist states that the clinic cancelled, **Then** the status becomes cancelled by the clinic. 5. **Given** a rescheduled or cancelled appointment, **When** the change is saved, **Then** the patient notice and reminder change are requested from messaging (feature 007). 6. **Given** an appointment that is arrived or no-show, **When** the receptionist opens its panel, **Then** reschedule and cancel are not offered. ---

items.title: Dentist sees their own day
