items.title: Confirmations, reminders, STOP and SMS fallback
items.description_md: Message templates, confirmations, 24-hour reminders with quiet hours, channel adapters for SMS/WhatsApp, STOP, WhatsApp-to-SMS fallback, reminders-failed list.

items.title: Patient gets a confirmation when booking or changing
items.description_md: A patient books an appointment online (or reception books it for them). At once, in the channel chosen for the appointment, they receive a confirmation that names the clinic, dentist, treatment, date and time, and gives a link to the appointment. When the patient cancels or reschedules, they receive a change notice in the same channel that says what changed. **Why this priority**: The confirmation is the patient's proof of the booking and the first message in the no-show chain. Without it the booking flow is not complete at go-live. **Independent Test**: Book an appointment against a sandbox provider account for each channel; check that one confirmation per booking arrives in the chosen channel with the six items. Cancel and reschedule it and check that one change notice arrives for each. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient who chose SMS, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** one SMS confirmation is sent within about 30 seconds with the clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time (in IST) and a link to the appointment. 2. **Given** a patient who chose WhatsApp, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the confirmation is sent through WhatsApp with the same content. 3. **Given** a booking that fails (for example the slot was taken), **When** the patient is told the slot is gone, **Then** no confirmation is sent. 4. **Given** the message provider is down when a booking is made, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the booking still succeeds and the confirmation is sent as soon as the provider recovers. 5. **Given** a patient who has switched reminders off, **When** they book, **Then** they still receive the confirmation. 6. **Given** an appointment that is cancelled or rescheduled, **When** the change is saved, **Then** one change notice is sent in the chosen channel (for a reschedule it shows the new clinic, dentist, date and time). ---

user_story.i_want: to receive a confirmation in my chosen channel when I book, cancel or reschedule an appointment
user_story.so_that: I have proof of the booking (clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time, link) and know exactly what changed

Given a patient who has switched reminders off, When they book, Then they still receive the confirmation. (source: FR-031)

Given an appointment that is cancelled or rescheduled, When the change is saved, Then one change notice is sent in the chosen channel (for a reschedule it shows the new clinic, dentist, date and time). (source: FR-018, FR-031)

items.title: Patient gets a reminder 24 hours before, never at night
items.description_md: A patient with an appointment booked at least 24 hours ahead receives a reminder 24 hours before the start, in the channel they chose. It says the clinic, dentist, date and time and has a link to reschedule or cancel. A reminder that would fall between 21:00 and 08:00 India time is sent at 20:00 instead, so no patient is messaged at night. **Why this priority**: This is the core feature that reduces no-shows. **Independent Test**: Create appointments whose reminders fall due in daytime, in the 21:00-24:00 window and in the 00:00-08:00 window, and book some close to the due time; with a controllable clock check that each reminder is sent at the expected time in the chosen channel with the required content. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an appointment on Tuesday 11:00, **When** Monday 11:00 IST arrives, **Then** one reminder is sent in the chosen channel stating clinic, dentist, date, time and a link to reschedule or cancel. 2. **Given** an appointment on Tuesday 22:30 (reminder due Monday 22:30), **When** Monday 20:00 IST arrives, **Then** the reminder is sent at 20:00 on Monday. 3. **Given** an appointment on Tuesday 03:00 (reminder due Monday 03:00), **When** Sunday 20:00 IST arrives, **Then** the reminder is sent at Sunday 20:00, the evening before the due day. 4. **Given** an appointment on Tuesday 08:00 (reminder due Monday 08:00, the end of quiet hours), **When** Monday 08:00 IST arrives, **Then** the reminder is sent at 08:00. 5. **Given** a booking made on Monday 20:30 for Tuesday 22:00 (due Monday 22:00, adjusted time 20:00 already passed, now outside quiet hours), **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the reminder is sent at once. 6. **Given** a booking made on Monday 21:15 for Tuesday 22:00 (adjusted time passed, now inside quiet hours), **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the reminder is sent at 08:00 on Tuesday. 7. **Given** a reminder, **When** it is built, **Then** the time shown is in IST and the text comes from the single English catalogue. ---

user_story.i_want: to get a reminder 24 hours before my appointment, never between 21:00 and 08:00
user_story.so_that: I remember to attend or reschedule without being messaged at night

items.title: No wrong reminders: cancelled, rescheduled and short-notice appointments
items.description_md: A patient is never reminded of an appointment that no longer exists. A cancelled appointment gets no reminder, even if the reminder was already queued. A rescheduled appointment gets one reminder, for its new time only. An appointment booked less than 24 hours ahead gets only the confirmation. **Why this priority**: A reminder for a cancelled visit would confuse patients and damage trust; NFR-005 requires zero of them. **Independent Test**: With a controllable clock, cancel, reschedule and short-notice-book appointments around the time their reminders are due and verify what is sent. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an appointment with a queued reminder, **When** the appointment is cancelled by the patient, by reception or by the clinic, **Then** the reminder is never sent. 2. **Given** a reminder that is due now but not yet sent, **When** the appointment is cancelled one second before the send attempt, **Then** the send is skipped because the appointment is checked again immediately before sending. 3. **Given** an appointment with a queued reminder, **When** it is rescheduled to a new time at least 24 hours away, **Then** the old reminder is dropped and exactly one reminder exists, for the new time. 4. **Given** an appointment rescheduled to a time less than 24 hours away, **When** the change is saved, **Then** the old reminder is dropped, no new reminder is created and only the change notice is sent. 5. **Given** an appointment booked less than 24 hours before its start, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** only the confirmation is sent and no reminder is ever created. 6. **Given** a reminder that has already been sent, **When** the appointment is later rescheduled, **Then** a new reminder is created for the new time (if 24 hours or more away). ---

user_story.i_want: never to be reminded of an appointment that was cancelled, moved or booked at short notice
user_story.so_that: I am not confused by wrong reminders and keep trusting the clinic's messages

Given an appointment booked less than 24 hours before its start, When the booking is saved, Then only the confirmation is sent and no reminder is ever created. (source: FR-028)
Given a reminder that has already been sent, When the appointment is later rescheduled, Then a new reminder is created for the new time (if 24 hours or more away). (source: FR-028)

items.title: Patient or reception can stop reminders
items.description_md: A patient replies STOP to a message and from then on gets no more reminders. Or the patient asks reception, who switches reminders off in the patient's record. Confirmations, change notices and sign-in codes are still sent. **Why this priority**: Required by Indian messaging rules (NFR-011) and by the patient's right to stop being messaged. It must work at go-live. **Independent Test**: Send a signed STOP reply from a sandbox number, then check that queued reminders for that account are skipped while a new booking still produces a confirmation. Repeat by switching the setting off as reception. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient with a queued reminder, **When** a genuine STOP reply from their phone number is received, **Then** their reminders are switched off and the queued reminder is not sent. 2. **Given** reception is on the patient's record, **When** the receptionist switches reminders off, **Then** no further reminders are sent for that patient account. 3. **Given** reminders are off for a patient, **When** the patient books, reschedules or cancels, **Then** the confirmation or change notice is still sent. 4. **Given** a STOP reply, **When** it is received, **Then** it takes effect within 1 hour at the latest (the design target is at once). 5. **Given** a STOP notification that is not properly signed or comes from a number with no account, **When** it arrives, **Then** it is rejected or ignored and no setting changes. 6. **Given** reminders are off, **When** reception switches them back on at the patient's request, **Then** reminders are sent again for appointments that are still 24 hours or more away. (source: FR-031; see Assumptions) ---

user_story.i_want: to stop reminders by replying STOP or by asking reception to switch them off
user_story.so_that: I am no longer messaged when I do not want to be, while still getting confirmations and sign-in codes

items.title: Reminders are on time and compliant, even when a provider has problems
items.description_md: The clinic's operator can rely on 99% of due reminders being sent within 15 minutes of their (adjusted) due time, on none being sent for cancelled appointments, and on every message going out only through registered templates. When a provider is slow or down, messages wait and are retried rather than being lost or duplicated, and the team is alerted when messages are late. **Why this priority**: This is the measurable goal of the whole feature (NFR-005) and a legal condition for sending (NFR-011). **Independent Test**: Run a simulated day of reminders against a provider stub that is slow, failing or repeating notifications; verify timeliness, no duplicates, no sends for cancelled appointments, alert on lag, and that nothing is sent without a registered template. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** normal load, **When** reminders fall due, **Then** at least 99% in a month are sent within 15 minutes of their adjusted due time. 2. **Given** the provider times out or errors, **When** a message is sent, **Then** it is retried (3 attempts, waiting 5 s then 30 s between them) and stays queued if the provider is still unavailable, rather than being dropped. 3. **Given** many consecutive provider failures (5 within 1 minute), **When** further messages are due, **Then** sending to that provider pauses briefly and messages stay queued, and sending resumes when the provider recovers. 4. **Given** the same message is processed twice (restart, two API instances, repeated provider notification), **When** it is sent, **Then** the patient receives it only once, and a repeated delivery receipt changes nothing. 5. **Given** the oldest due, unsent message is more than 10 minutes late, **When** the lag is measured, **Then** an alert is raised. 6. **Given** the nightly check, **When** it finds an appointment that should have a reminder but has none, or a message stuck in progress, **Then** it repairs it and reports the count. 7. **Given** any message to be sent, **When** its kind and channel have no approved template configured, **Then** it is not sent and the problem is reported; SMS goes only through the registered sender ID and DLT templates, and WhatsApp only through approved templates. 8. **Given** a provider call, **When** it is made, **Then** only the templated values (clinic, dentist, date, time, link) and the phone number are sent, and no patient name, phone number or message text appears in logs. 9. **Given** a delivery receipt that is unsigned or refers to an unknown message, **When** it arrives, **Then** it is rejected or ignored. 10. **Given** messages older than 90 days, **When** the retention job runs, **Then** they are deleted. ---

user_story.i_want: due reminders to go out within 15 minutes, once only, through registered templates, even when a provider is slow or down
user_story.so_that: no-shows fall and the clinic stays compliant with Indian messaging rules

items.title: Provider accounts and templates are registered and ready before go-live
items.description_md: The delivery team and the clinic get the SMS provider and WhatsApp provider accounts, the DLT registration (sender ID and templates) and the WhatsApp template approvals started early, so that confirmations, reminders and sign-in codes can go live on 1 March 2027. Staging works against provider sandbox accounts. **Why this priority**: If registration or approval is late, confirmations, reminders and sign-in codes cannot go live (RSK-001). Lead times are outside our control, so this work starts first. **Independent Test**: Check that the template catalogue is written and submitted, that sandbox accounts work in staging, and that a go-live readiness check in production configuration reports every template as approved and configured. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the message kinds and channels, **When** the template catalogue is reviewed, **Then** there is one English template for each kind and channel in use, each using only the allowed fields, ready for submission. 2. **Given** the catalogue, **When** the clinic (with our help) submits DLT registration and the WhatsApp templates, **Then** each submission, date, owner and status is tracked. 3. **Given** staging, **When** a booking is made, **Then** messages go to provider sandbox accounts and never to real patients. 4. **Given** the production configuration, **When** the readiness check runs, **Then** it lists any template that is not approved or has no identifier configured, and the go-live decision uses that list. 5. **Given** the chosen providers are not yet decided, **When** the work starts, **Then** the provider-specific parts are isolated in one adapter per provider so a provider can be replaced without changing the rest. (source: NFR-011; see Assumptions) ---

items.title: Sign-in code is sent by SMS straight away
items.description_md: The sign-in feature asks this feature to send a one-time code by SMS to a phone number. The code is sent during the request (not queued), so the patient sees at once whether it was sent. It goes through the registered SMS sender ID and template. **Why this priority**: Patients cannot sign in, and so cannot book, without the code (feature 002 depends on this). **Independent Test**: Call the sending capability with a sandbox number; check that the SMS arrives from the registered template and that a provider failure is reported back to the caller immediately. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the sign-in feature requests a code for a phone number, **When** the request is made, **Then** the SMS is sent during that request and the caller learns at once whether the provider accepted it. 2. **Given** the SMS provider is down or times out, **When** a code is requested, **Then** the caller gets a clear "could not send" result within the timeout and the code is not queued for later delivery. 3. **Given** a sign-in code message, **When** it is recorded, **Then** the code itself is not kept in readable form in the message record or any log. 4. **Given** a patient who has switched reminders off, **When** they request a code, **Then** the code is still sent. ---

items.title: Undelivered WhatsApp reminder is sent once by SMS (Release 2)
items.description_md: When a WhatsApp reminder cannot be delivered, the patient gets it once by SMS instead. If the SMS also fails, the appointment is marked "reminder failed". The fallback is built behind a switch that is on by default, because the client has not yet agreed to it. **Why this priority**: Release 2 (Should). A reminder that never arrives defeats the goal, but the MVP can go live without it. The client has not agreed to the fallback (ISS-001, ASM-005), so it must be switchable. **Independent Test**: With the switch on, make the WhatsApp sandbox fail a reminder and check that exactly one SMS follows; make SMS fail too and check the appointment is marked "reminder failed". Turn the switch off and repeat. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a WhatsApp reminder that cannot be delivered (provider error after retries, or a failed delivery receipt) and the fallback switch on, **When** the failure is known, **Then** one SMS reminder with the same content is sent to the same patient. 2. **Given** a failed-receipt notification is repeated or replayed, **When** it arrives again, **Then** no second SMS is created. 3. **Given** the SMS fallback also fails, **When** the failure is known, **Then** the appointment is marked "reminder failed". 4. **Given** the fallback switch is off, **When** a WhatsApp reminder cannot be delivered, **Then** no SMS is sent and the appointment is marked "reminder failed". (source: FR-029; see Assumptions) 5. **Given** a patient who chose SMS and the SMS reminder fails, **When** the failure is known, **Then** the appointment is marked "reminder failed" and no other message is sent. 6. **Given** the fallback SMS is sent, **When** the patient has replied STOP in the meantime or the appointment has been cancelled, **Then** the SMS is not sent. 7. **Given** a WhatsApp reminder that is delivered, **When** the receipt arrives, **Then** no SMS is sent. ---

user_story.i_want: a WhatsApp reminder that could not be delivered to be sent once by SMS instead
user_story.so_that: I still get my reminder and do not miss the appointment

Given a failed-receipt notification is repeated or replayed, When it arrives again, Then no second SMS is created. (source: FR-029)
Given the SMS fallback also fails, When the failure is known, Then the appointment is marked "reminder failed". (source: FR-029)
Given the fallback switch is off, When a WhatsApp reminder cannot be delivered, Then no SMS is sent and the appointment is marked "reminder failed". (source: FR-029; see Assumptions)
Given a patient who chose SMS and the SMS reminder fails, When the failure is known, Then the appointment is marked "reminder failed" and no other message is sent. (source: FR-029)
Given the fallback SMS is sent, When the patient has replied STOP in the meantime or the appointment has been cancelled, Then the SMS is not sent. (source: FR-029, FR-028, FR-031)
Given a WhatsApp reminder that is delivered, When the receipt arrives, Then no SMS is sent. (source: FR-029)

estimate.rationale: 5 tasks: expand-only migration, model columns, idempotent fallback logic, wiring into dispatcher and receipts; 7 scenarios.

open_questions: The client has not agreed to the SMS fallback (ISS-001, ASM-005); it is built behind WHATSAPP_SMS_FALLBACK_ENABLED, default on. Confirm before Release 2 (DL-2).

items.title: Reception sees tomorrow's failed reminders (Release 2)
items.description_md: In the afternoon, a receptionist opens the "Reminders failed" screen and sees tomorrow's appointments, at their own clinic, whose reminder could not be delivered by any channel. They phone those patients. **Why this priority**: Release 2 (Should). It gives reception a safety net for the patients the system could not reach. **Independent Test**: Create tomorrow's appointments with failed, delivered, cancelled and not-reminded states at two clinics, sign in as a receptionist of one clinic and check the list. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** tomorrow has appointments marked "reminder failed", **When** a receptionist opens "Reminders failed", **Then** they see exactly those appointments at their own clinic with time, patient name, phone number, dentist, treatment and chosen channel. 2. **Given** a failed-reminder appointment is cancelled, **When** the list is refreshed, **Then** it no longer appears. 3. **Given** a receptionist of one clinic, **When** they open the list, **Then** they never see another clinic's appointments; the practice manager sees both clinics. 4. **Given** appointments whose reminders were delivered, are still queued, or were never created (booked less than 24 hours ahead), **When** the list is shown, **Then** they do not appear. 5. **Given** no reminder failed for tomorrow, **When** the list is opened, **Then** an empty state says so. 6. **Given** the Release 2 feature flag is off, **When** a user looks for the screen, **Then** it is not shown. ---

items.description_md: Patient adds up to 5 family members and books for them; each booking names the person.

items.title: Add family members to my account
items.description_md: A signed-in patient opens "Family" on their account and adds a family member by giving a name and a birth year. They can add up to 5 family members. The new person shows in the list of people on the account, next to the patient themselves. The family member has no phone number and no sign-in of their own: they are a person on the account holder's account. **Why this priority**: Nothing else in this feature works until a family member exists. It is the core of FR-006. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a patient with no family members, add one with a name and birth year, and see them in the list. Add four more; the sixth attempt is refused with a clear message. Delivers a usable list of people on the account. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient with fewer than 5 family members, **When** they enter a name and a valid birth year and confirm, **Then** the family member is saved on their account and appears in the list of people on the account. 2. **Given** a signed-in patient who already has 5 family members, **When** they try to add another, **Then** the system refuses, says that 5 family members is the limit, and the list is unchanged. 3. **Given** a signed-in patient on the add screen, **When** they leave the name empty or enter a birth year that is not a four-digit year in a plausible range, **Then** the system says what to correct and saves nothing. 4. **Given** a signed-in patient, **When** they add a family member, **Then** only a name and a birth year are stored for that person (no phone number, no other personal details). 5. **Given** the family-members feature flag is off, **When** a patient opens their account or sends a request to add a family member, **Then** the "Family" screen is not shown and the request is refused. ---

user_story.i_want: to add up to 5 family members (name and birth year) to my account
user_story.so_that: I can book and manage visits for my family from one place

Given the family-members feature flag is off, When a patient opens their account or sends a request to add a family member, Then the "Family" screen is not shown and the request is refused. (source: FR-006)

items.title: Choose who the visit is for when booking
items.description_md: When a signed-in patient books online, the first choice is who the visit is for: themselves or one of their family members. The booking is saved against that person. The rest of the booking flow (clinic, treatment, dentist, slot, channel) is unchanged. A patient with no family members is not asked an extra question, and books for themselves as before. **Why this priority**: This is the reason the patient adds family members: booking for them. Each booking must name the person it is for (FR-006). **Independent Test**: With a patient who has two family members, book a visit for a family member and check that the confirmation and the appointment name that person. Book one for the patient themselves and check that it names the patient. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient with at least one family member and the flag on, **When** they start a booking, **Then** they are asked who the visit is for and the choices are themselves and each of their family members. 2. **Given** the patient chose a family member, **When** they complete the booking, **Then** the appointment is saved for that family member, the booked screen and the confirmation name that person, and the booking takes no more screens than a booking for the patient themselves plus the one "who is it for" choice. 3. **Given** a signed-in patient with no family members, **When** they start a booking, **Then** the visit is for themselves and no "who is it for" question is shown. 4. **Given** a signed-in patient, **When** a request names a person who is not on that patient's account, **Then** the system refuses it and no appointment is created. 5. **Given** the family-members flag is off, **When** a patient books, **Then** the booking is for the patient themselves and no family choice is offered. ---

items.title: See family members' appointments in my list
items.description_md: A signed-in patient sees, in "My appointments", the upcoming and past appointments of themselves and of their family members, each with the name of the person it is for and its status. A patient never sees appointments of people outside their own account. **Why this priority**: It lets the account holder manage the family's visits. FR-004 and FR-015 already say the list includes family members; this story makes it true once family members exist. **Independent Test**: Book one visit for the patient and one for a family member, open "My appointments" and see both, each naming its person. Sign in as a different patient and see neither. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient and a family member each have an upcoming appointment, **When** the patient opens "My appointments", **Then** both appear, each showing the person it is for and its status. 2. **Given** a family member has a past appointment, **When** the patient opens the past appointments, **Then** it is listed with the family member's name and its status. 3. **Given** two different accounts, **When** one patient opens their list or asks for an appointment of the other account, **Then** the other account's appointments are never shown and the request is refused. 4. **Given** a patient opens an appointment of a family member, **When** they reschedule or cancel it under the rules of the appointment features, **Then** the same rules apply as for their own appointments. ---

user_story.i_want: to see the appointments of myself and my family members in My appointments, each with the person's name and status
user_story.so_that: I can keep track of and change the whole family's visits in one list

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a patient and a family member each have an upcoming appointment, When the patient opens "My appointments", Then both appear, each showing the person it is for and its status. (source: FR-004, FR-015, FR-006)
Given a family member has a past appointment, When the patient opens the past appointments, Then it is listed with the family member's name and its status. (source: FR-015)

Given two different accounts, When one patient opens their list or asks for an appointment of the other account, Then the other account's appointments are never shown and the request is refused. (source: FR-004, NFR-006)

Given a patient opens an appointment of a family member, When they reschedule or cancel it under the rules of the appointment features, Then the same rules apply as for their own appointments. (source: FR-004, FR-015)

items.title: Messages for a family member's visit reach the account's phone
items.description_md: When a visit is booked for a family member, the confirmation, the change notice and the reminder go to the account's phone number in the account's chosen channel (SMS or WhatsApp). The message names the person the visit is for. Family members have no phone number or channel of their own. If the account has switched reminders off, no reminder goes for any person on the account, as for the account holder. **Why this priority**: Without it the account holder cannot tell which family visit a message is about. It reuses the existing messaging; the change is the person's name in the message and the account-level addressing. **Independent Test**: Book a visit for a family member, check that the confirmation arrives at the account's phone in the chosen channel and names the family member. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a visit booked for a family member, **When** the confirmation is sent, **Then** it goes to the account's phone number in the channel chosen for that booking and names the family member. 2. **Given** a reminder is due for a family member's appointment, **When** it is sent, **Then** it goes to the account's phone number in the account's channel and names the family member. 3. **Given** the account has reminders switched off, **When** a reminder falls due for a family member's appointment, **Then** no reminder is sent but confirmations and change notices still are. ---

user_story.as_a: patient (P-01) who books for a family member
user_story.i_want: confirmations, change notices and reminders for their visit to reach my phone and name the person
user_story.so_that: I can tell which family visit each message is about

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a visit booked for a family member, When the confirmation is sent, Then it goes to the account's phone number in the channel chosen for that booking and names the family member. (source: FR-006, FR-014)
Given a reminder is due for a family member's appointment, When it is sent, Then it goes to the account's phone number in the account's channel and names the family member. (source: FR-006, FR-027)
Given the account has reminders switched off, When a reminder falls due for a family member's appointment, Then no reminder is sent but confirmations and change notices still are. (source: FR-031)

items.title: Repeat no-show block and no-show report (Release 2)
items.description_md: Block online booking after 2 no-shows in 6 months, lift by reception, monthly no-show report per clinic.

items.title: A patient with 2 recent no-shows cannot book or reschedule online
items.description_md: A patient (or a family member the patient books for) who has had 2 no-shows in the last 6 months is told, when they try to book or reschedule online, that online booking is not available and is shown the clinic's phone number. Appointments they already have stay as they are. Each person is counted on their own: a family member's no-shows count against that family member, not against the account holder. **Why this priority**: This is the rule that discourages repeat no-shows, the clinic's biggest problem. Without it the other two stories have nothing to show or lift. **Independent Test**: Record 2 no-shows within 6 months for one test patient, then sign in as that patient and try to book and to reschedule; both are refused with the clinic phone number, while an existing booking is still listed and can be cancelled. Repeat for a family member on the same account and confirm the account holder is not blocked. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months, **When** they reach the step where they choose a dentist and slot, **Then** the system says online booking is not available and shows the phone number of the clinic they chose, and no booking is created. 2. **Given** a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months and an upcoming booking, **When** they try to reschedule it online, **Then** the system says online rescheduling is not available and shows the phone number of that appointment's clinic, and the booking stays unchanged. 3. **Given** a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months and upcoming bookings, **When** they view their appointments, **Then** all existing bookings are still listed and none is cancelled or changed by the block. 4. **Given** an account holder with a family member who has 2 no-shows in the last 6 months, **When** the account holder books online for themselves, **Then** the booking is accepted; **When** they try to book for that family member, **Then** it is refused as in scenario 1. 5. **Given** a patient with 1 no-show in the last 6 months, **When** they book or reschedule online, **Then** the booking proceeds as normal. 6. **Given** a patient whose older no-show falls out of the 6-month window so that fewer than 2 remain in the window, **When** they try to book online, **Then** the booking proceeds as normal without anyone lifting anything. 7. **Given** the Release 2 feature flag is off, **When** a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months books or reschedules, **Then** the booking behaves as before this feature (not blocked). ---

user_story.as_a: patient (P-01) who books for myself or a family member
user_story.i_want: to be told clearly, with the clinic's phone number, when online booking or rescheduling is not available to me after 2 no-shows in 6 months, while my existing bookings stay
user_story.so_that: I know to phone the clinic, and the clinic's repeat no-shows are discouraged without losing appointments I already have

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months, When they reach the step where they choose a dentist and slot, Then the system says online booking is not available and shows the phone number of the clinic they chose, and no booking is created

Given a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months and an upcoming booking, When they try to reschedule it online, Then the system says online rescheduling is not available and shows the phone number of that appointment's clinic, and the booking stays unchanged

Given a patient with 2 no-shows in the last 6 months and upcoming bookings, When they view their appointments, Then all existing bookings are still listed and none is cancelled or changed by the block

items.title: Reception sees a block and lifts it
items.description_md: A receptionist opening a patient's record sees that the patient is blocked from online booking. When a blocked patient phones and the clinic agrees, the receptionist lifts the block. Lifting starts the patient's no-show count again from zero, and the lift records who did it and when. **Why this priority**: A block with no way out would turn away patients for good and flood reception with complaints. Lifting must ship with the block. **Independent Test**: Block a test patient, open their record as a receptionist and confirm the block is shown, lift it, then confirm the patient can book online again, that the lift is recorded with the receptionist and time, and that one new no-show does not block them but a second new one does. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a blocked patient, **When** a receptionist opens that patient's record or an appointment panel for that patient, **Then** the screen clearly shows the patient is blocked from online booking and since when. 2. **Given** a blocked patient, **When** the receptionist lifts the block, **Then** the patient can book and reschedule online straight away, and the system records the receptionist and the time of the lift. 3. **Given** a patient whose block was just lifted, **When** one new no-show is recorded, **Then** the patient is not blocked; **When** a second new no-show is recorded after the lift, **Then** the patient is blocked again. 4. **Given** a patient who had 2 no-shows before a lift and none after, **When** the system counts their no-shows, **Then** the count is zero. 5. **Given** a patient who is not blocked, **When** a receptionist opens their record, **Then** no lift action is offered. 6. **Given** a blocked patient, **When** a receptionist books an appointment for them at the desk or by phone, **Then** the booking is accepted, because the block applies to online booking and rescheduling only. 7. **Given** a patient is blocked because of a no-show marked today, **When** the receptionist undoes that no-show the same day and the patient then has fewer than 2 no-shows in the window, **Then** the block no longer applies and no lift record is created. ---

user_story.so_that: a blocked patient who phones can book online again, the count restarts from zero, and who lifted it and when is on record

items.title: The practice manager reads the no-show report per clinic and month
items.description_md: The practice manager opens a no-show report that shows, for each clinic and for each of the last 12 months, the number of no-shows and the no-show rate (no-shows divided by appointments that were not cancelled). The report is on screen only, with no export. **Why this priority**: It gives the manager the figure the clinic lacks today and the baseline for the TBD no-show target (ASM-015). It does not depend on the block, so it can ship and be tested on its own, but patients and reception feel the block first. **Independent Test**: Seed appointments across 2 clinics and several months with a known mix of statuses, open the report as the practice manager, and compare each clinic-month cell with hand-counted figures; confirm a receptionist and a patient cannot open it and that no export action exists. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the practice manager is signed in, **When** they open the no-show report, **Then** they see one row per clinic and month for the last 12 months, each with the number of no-shows and the no-show rate. 2. **Given** a clinic-month with 40 appointments of which 4 were cancelled by the patient, 2 cancelled by the clinic and 3 are no-shows, **When** the report is shown, **Then** the rate is 3 divided by 34 (appointments not cancelled), shown as a percentage, and the no-show count is 3. 3. **Given** a walk-in booked as a normal appointment and marked arrived, **When** the report counts that month, **Then** the walk-in is counted among the appointments that were not cancelled. 4. **Given** a clinic-month with no appointments that were not cancelled, **When** the report is shown, **Then** the count is 0 and the rate is shown as "no appointments" rather than as a number or an error. 5. **Given** a patient whose personal data was deleted on request and whose appointment rows were anonymised, **When** the report is shown, **Then** the counts and rates are the same as before the deletion. 6. **Given** a receptionist or a patient or a dentist is signed in, **When** they try to open the report, **Then** access is refused. 7. **Given** the report is open, **When** the manager looks for a way to download or export it, **Then** none is offered. 8. **Given** the Release 2 feature flag is off, **When** the practice manager looks at the menu, **Then** the report screen is not shown. ---
